name: Regime-armed momentum with RSI-not-overbought guard (gate is macro, not the RSI ceiling)
rationale: THESIS: macro_regime decides WHETHER to trust the tape; rsi decides whether the entry PRICE is over-extended. In a risk-on regime I want to ride trend, but chasing a vertically overbought print (RSI near the top) pays for the worst part of the move. So I arm momentum only when macro_regime>floor AND ret_Nd>mom_floor AND rsi<rsi_ceiling — trend confirmed, macro window open, but not yet euphorically stretched. The macro gate is the orthogonal piece; the RSI ceiling is just price-discipline. DISCONFIRMER: run the SAME entry with macro_regime DROPPED but the rsi<rsi_ceiling guard kept (RSI-gated momentum). If the RSI-only version reproduces the macro+RSI net-of-fee Sharpe, the macro gate is redundant to a mechanical not-overbought filter and carries no macro information — falsified. The macro gate must add incremental net edge over the RSI-only version. Low turnover because the RSI ceiling avoids repeatedly re-entering froth.
catalyst: Risk-on macro regime with confirmed positive trend but RSI still below its overbought ceiling — the window arms a non-stretched momentum entry.
